title: One Ångström Across 315,000 Years of Pan-African Homo sapiens — Jean-Jacques Hublin's 315-ka Jebel Irhoud Skulls & Pan-African Metapopulation Evolution, 73-100 ka Blombos Cave Ochre Workshop, Holly Dunsworth & Herman Pontzer's 2.1-2.5x BMR EGG Hypothesis Overturning Washburn's Obstetrical Dilemma & Placental hCG/HbF (PDB 1HRP, 7FIH, 1FDH, 4MQJ, 3EQM)

teenKit.tldr: Forget the old textbook lie that narrow hips limit human baby size—the real limit is your mother's maximum daily calorie-burning capacity, enforced at the atomic level inside the placenta.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how our ancestors evolved across a vast African network and how our metabolism drives pregnancy changes how modern medicine approaches fetal health and metabolic limits.
keyTakeaways: Human origins weren't a single 'Cradle of Humankind' in East Africa, but a massive, continent-spanning network of interacting populations sharing genes and culture for over 315,000 years.
The famous 'Obstetrical Dilemma'—the idea that walking upright forced narrow hips and premature, helpless babies—has been completely busted because wider hips don't slow you down or waste energy.
The actual invisible wall forcing birth at 39 weeks is the 'Energetics of Gestation and Growth' (EGG) hypothesis, governed by how much energy a mother's metabolism can pump into the placenta.

vocab.meaning: A vast, interconnected web of ancient human groups across the African continent that occasionally swapped genes and culture rather than evolving in one isolated spot.
The mid-century mid-set myth that human birth is dangerous because bipedal walking requires narrow pelvises, which was proven false by treadmill tests.
The scientific model showing that pregnancy ends at roughly 40 weeks not because of hip space, but because a mother hits her absolute limit of daily metabolic energy output.
An ultra-tiny unit of measurement equal to one ten-billionth of a meter, used to examine molecules and atomic structures inside the placenta.

quiz.question: What did researchers discover when they tested the classic Obstetrical Dilemma on a treadmill?
options: Wider hips significantly slow down bipedal walking and waste huge amounts of energy.
Wider hips do not slow you down or cost you any extra energy at all.
Walking upright is physically impossible for anyone with broad hips.
Chimpanzees walk much more efficiently than humans.
quiz.explanation: Treadmill experiments proved that wider hips impose zero metabolic penalty, completely destroying the traditional hip-constraint theory.

quiz.question: According to the EGG hypothesis, what is the actual limiting factor that forces human labor around 39 to 40 weeks?
options: The absolute maximum number of calories a mother's metabolism can safely burn per day to fuel the fetus.
The physical stretching limit of human skin.
The exact size of the human pelvic bone opening.
The baby's brain volume reaching the skull's maximum physical capacity.
quiz.explanation: Pregnancy ends when the energy demands of the growing fetus push past the mother's peak daily metabolic ceiling (roughly 2.1 to 2.5 times her baseline resting metabolic rate).

quiz.question: How do modern scientists view the origin of Homo sapiens across Africa 315,000 years ago based on sites like Jebel Irhoud?
options: A single isolated tribe in East Africa that suddenly replaced everyone else.
A miraculous single mutation event in a cave in South Africa.
A sprawling, continent-wide network of populations sharing genes, tools, and ideas across long distances.
An offshoot of Neanderthals who migrated south during an ice age.
quiz.explanation: Fossil and archaeological evidence point to a pan-African metapopulation—a connected network of groups interacting across the continent over hundreds of thousands of years.
